column5: short day, much work, pressing master
column6: The commentary's asr is a late, pressing interval in which deeds must be done; Rabbi Tarfon pictures a short day, much work, workers and a pressing master in one labour account.

column5: self, others and the present hour
column6: The commentary moves from an isolated endangered person into mutual responsibility under dwindling time; Hillel asks what he is if only for himself and, finally, if not now, when.

column5: Rahab's red cord read as redemptive blood
column6: The commentary's cord marks a household's rescue from destruction; 1 Clement reads the scarlet cord as a sign of redemption through the Lord's blood, changing a rescue marker into a Christian theological sign.

column5: strong sustain weak and rich provide for poor
column6: The commentary makes the steep path communal with burdens and feeding; Clement urges strong people to care for weak people and wealthy people to provide for poor people.

column5: vine and supporting elm represent reciprocal aid
column6: The commentary's productive vine and joined community meet in Hermas's vine that bears fruit with the elm's support; the allegory applies this to rich and poor helping each other materially and in prayer.

column5: captives fed, clothed and carried on donkeys
column6: The commentary's ascent joins freed prisoners, food, a load animal and restored company; Judean captives are clothed, fed, anointed and carried on donkeys back to their kin.

column5: return captive brothers
column6: The commentary turns confinement and enmity into brotherhood; Oded calls the captives brothers and orders their captors to send them back.

column5: feed captured enemies instead of killing them
column6: The commentary's path frees those held and feeds the hungry; Elisha tells the king to give captured Arameans bread and water so they may return to their master.

column5: feast ends enemy raids
column6: The commentary moves from struggle to company through release and food; after the captured Arameans eat and leave, their raiding bands cease entering Israel.

column5: creditor threatens to enslave widow's sons
column6: The commentary makes debt, captivity and threatened family loss one scene; a widow says her creditor has come to take her two sons as slaves.

column5: oil sold to pay debt and sustain family
column6: The commentary joins pressed yield, rescue from debt and continuing provision; Elisha tells the widow to sell her oil, pay the creditor and live on the remainder.

column5: children enslaved through debt and lost fields
column6: The commentary's bad market strips a household of both future and freedom; Nehemiah's complainants say their children are forced into slavery while their fields and vineyards belong to others.

column5: restore vineyards and pledged goods
column6: The commentary links debt, fruit-bearing land and release from a creditor's hold; Nehemiah demands the immediate return of fields, vineyards and financial claims.

column5: vineyard gleanings left to poor and stranger
column6: The commentary's grapes and hunger belong to one ethical landscape; Leviticus leaves the ungleaned vineyard fruit for poor people and foreigners.

column5: forgotten harvest left for vulnerable people
column6: The commentary's stored yield meets an obligation to feed on the hard path; Deuteronomy leaves a forgotten sheaf to stranger, orphan and widow rather than reclaiming it.

column5: feed hungry and light rises in darkness
column6: The commentary links feeding, mutual care and the transition of night into day; Isaiah says satisfying the hungry makes darkness like noonday.

column5: well-watered garden whose waters do not fail
column6: The commentary's rain-grown garden faces devastating loss; Isaiah promises the one who feeds the afflicted an unfailing watered garden, the positive outcome of the same food scene.

column5: tree by water continues fruit in drought
column6: The commentary's lifetime garden fails under destructive weather; Jeremiah's trusting person is a rooted tree whose leaves stay green and fruit continues even in drought.

column5: wages put into a bag with holes
column6: The commentary pictures a person's principal steadily eroding; Haggai names meagre harvest and wages that disappear as though stored in a perforated purse.

column5: giving increases, withholding causes want
column6: The commentary's bad exchange loses capital whereas shared goods preserve a community; Proverbs reverses ordinary accounting by contrasting generous increase with possessive want.

column5: one who waters others is watered
column6: The commentary's rain and preserved yield become reciprocal support; Proverbs makes refreshment flow back to the person who refreshes others.

column5: feeding poor treated as a loan repaid by God
column6: The commentary puts debt and support of the needy together; Proverbs casts kindness to a poor person as lending to the Lord, who repays.

column5: give bread to a hungry enemy
column6: The commentary moves from contest to shared sustenance; Proverbs specifically orders feeding and watering an enemy in need.

column5: rescue people being taken to death
column6: The commentary's hard ascent includes releasing someone held at a lethal edge; Proverbs commands intervention for people being led to death.

column5: God weighs hearts and repays rescue omitted
column6: The commentary sets the rescue duty beside weighing and final recompense; the following proverb rejects the excuse of ignorance because the keeper of souls weighs hearts and repays deeds.

column5: false commercial scales cannot be acquitted
column6: The commentary joins the market, truthful measurement and light weight in judgment; Micah asks whether wicked scales and deceitful weights could be treated as innocent.

column5: dishonest balance versus just weight
column6: The commentary's market bargain meets the scale that tests moral worth; Proverbs opposes fraudulent scales to an accurate weight pleasing to God.

column5: poor bought for silver while grain is sold
column6: The commentary's wrong bargain intersects hunger and bondage; Amos condemns merchants who sell grain while buying the needy for silver and the poor for sandals.

column5: kingdom's numbered days brought to an end
column6: The commentary places human loss inside spent time before the next verse's scale; Daniel first interprets the writing as Belshazzar's numbered, completed reign.

column5: fruitful tree by streams that does not wither
column6: The commentary's lost garden contrasts with faith and fruitful works; the righteous person is a planted tree yielding fruit in season whose leaf does not wither.

column5: former slave received as a brother
column6: The commentary's journey turns captivity and enmity into a community; Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus beyond the slave relationship as a beloved brother.

column5: charge a brother's debt to the intercessor
column6: The commentary joins release with debt and a guarantor; Paul offers to have anything Onesimus owes charged to Paul's own account.

column5: personal written promise to repay
column6: The commentary's testament scene ties written custody, obligation and faithful surety; Paul says he writes the repayment pledge with his own hand.

column5: Rahab's rescue linked to sheltering messengers
column6: The commentary's cord-marked house joins safety to deeds; James interprets Rahab's reception and dispatch of the messengers as active righteousness.

column5: Rahab's survival attributed to faith and welcome
column6: The commentary's rope and shared refuge secure a household; Hebrews reads Rahab's non-destruction through her faith and reception of the spies, adding a faith reading to the cord scene.

column5: vineyard labourers paid at evening
column6: The commentary treats the day as spent capital whose end reveals its yield; the vineyard owner orders wages paid when evening arrives.

column5: one late hour weighed against whole day of labour
column6: The commentary's late hour, work and rightful payment converge; early vineyard workers complain that the last workers' single hour received equal pay.

column5: storing for oneself versus true wealth
column6: The commentary says hoarded yield can be lost at the moment of use; Jesus concludes the rich fool's story by contrasting self-stored treasure with wealth toward God.

column5: give to poor and store imperishable treasure
column6: The commentary opposes spent principal to what is safely kept through mutual help; Jesus commands almsgiving and treasure where it does not fail.

column5: sell possessions and give to poor to gain treasure
column6: The commentary's hard ascent includes release from holding wealth and feeding the needy; Jesus tells the rich man to give his sale proceeds to poor people and follow him.

column5: rich instructed to do good and share readily
column6: The commentary moves from endangered capital into communal good works; Paul orders the rich to be generous and ready to share.

column5: sharing stores a firm foundation for future life
column6: The commentary turns spent capital into an enduring good through deeds; Paul says generous people store a foundation for the future and take hold of life.

column5: the day and fire test each person's work
column6: The commentary's later judgment exposes the value of fitted work; Paul says the day discloses each builder's work as fire tests its quality.

column5: love in deed and truth rather than words only
column6: The commentary refuses to separate mutual counsel of truth from rightly fitted acts; this verse expressly joins truth, action and love among siblings.

column5: support others and become fellow workers for truth
column6: The commentary has truth passed hand to hand in a working community; the letter says supporting travelling workers makes the supporters coworkers with truth.

column5: endurance gains life
column6: The commentary sets human loss against sabr as self-restraint and preservation; Jesus says his addressees will gain their lives through endurance amid persecution.

column5: works, labour and endurance named together
column6: The commentary closes with faith translated into good work and patience; the risen speaker says he knows the Ephesian assembly's works, labour and endurance.

column5: imprisonment tests faithfulness until death
column6: The commentary brings detention, patience and the end of life into one movement; the Smyrna assembly is warned of prison and urged to remain faithful unto death for the crown of life.

column5: kept word of endurance and promised protection
column6: The commentary's preserved essence is reciprocal fidelity under pressure; Christ says the assembly kept his word of endurance and promises to keep it from the coming hour of trial.

column5: withheld harvest wages cry out in judgment
column6: The commentary's orchard yield meets bad market accounting and the final day; James says field workers' withheld pay cries out against wealthy landowners.

column5: one group's surplus supplies another's lack
column6: The commentary turns loss into shared provision through reciprocal action; Paul describes present abundance covering another group's need and future reciprocity.

column5: members suffer and rejoice together
column6: The commentary moves from a solitary person into joined lives; Paul says all members suffer when one suffers and rejoice when one is honoured.

column5: freedom expressed by serving one another
column6: The commentary's released captive enters a community of mutual responsibility; Paul tells freed people to use freedom to serve one another in love.

column5: building fitted together and growing
column6: The commentary compares righteous works and persons to bricks settling in place; Paul says the whole structure is joined together and grows into a holy temple.

column5: joined body builds itself through each part's work
column6: The commentary's separate people become a working whole; Paul says each part contributes to the joined body's growth in love.

column5: gifts received and passed as entrusted service
column6: The commentary's truth and patience move between people like a kept trust; Peter calls each person to serve others with a received gift as a steward.

column5: outward wasting and daily inner renewal
column6: The commentary's human principal erodes during time while a substance is preserved; Paul describes the outer person wasting away as the inner person is renewed day by day.

column5: pressure produces eternal weight
column6: The commentary moves from pressure and light scales to enduring value; Paul says temporary affliction produces an incomparable eternal weight of glory.

column5: testing faith produces endurance
column6: The commentary treats sabr as the retained product of pressure on faith; James states that the testing of faith produces steadfastness.

column5: endurance completes its work
column6: The commentary joins patience to rightly fitted works; James lets endurance have its full work so a person becomes complete and lacking nothing.

column5: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
column6: The commentary says believers enter safety; Genesis says Abram believed the Lord and that trust was reckoned to him as righteousness, giving a specific faith-and-right-standing use of the corresponding root.

column5: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
column6: The commentary joins belief with a secure standing amid loss; Isaiah warns that unless his hearers trust, they will not be established, a Hebrew play on two forms of אמן.

column5: own recollection: Arabic آمنوا / Hebrew אמן
column6: The commentary's believers endure and do right; Habakkuk says the righteous person will live by faithfulness, applying the corresponding root to sustained fidelity under crisis.

column5: vine ripens before pressing dream
column6: The commentary links growing fruit with squeezing in Joseph's prison; the cupbearer's dream first presents a budding vine whose clusters ripen before the pressing action in Genesis 40:11.

column5: Joseph holds brothers in custody during famine
column6: The commentary makes Joseph's food rescue meet detention; Joseph confines his brothers for three days while testing those who seek grain.

column5: one brother detained while others carry food home
column6: The commentary joins alıkonma to sustenance; Joseph holds one brother as security and sends the others with grain for their hungry households.

column5: Joseph sent ahead to preserve survivors
column6: The commentary's good year turns pressing and food into communal rescue; Joseph interprets his arrival in Egypt as a means of preserving a remnant through famine.

column5: abandoned servant fed until revived
column6: The commentary's difficult road includes feeding and releasing the held or neglected person; David's men give an Egyptian bread, water and fruit after his master abandoned him.

column5: freed servants forcibly taken back
column6: The commentary's steep path releases a captive into fellowship; Jeremiah condemns people who reverse a prior manumission and bring their servants back into bondage.

column5: pledged garment returned by sunset
column6: The commentary's debt scene joins held collateral to a spent day; Exodus also requires returning a poor person's pledged cloak before the sun goes down.

column5: free yourself after becoming surety
column6: The commentary gives sabr a guarantor sense while its path frees the constrained; Proverbs depicts a debt guarantor caught in another's hand and urgently seeking release.

column5: giving poor yields enduring righteousness
column6: The commentary makes a shared gift survive the waste of time; the psalm says one who distributes to the poor has righteousness enduring forever.

column5: breath withers flower and grass
column6: The commentary's rain-grown fruit is exposed to destructive weather and passing life; Isaiah says the divine breath dries grass and fades flowers as an image of human frailty.

column5: word remains after vegetation fades
column6: The commentary ends with a preserved and transmitted essence after loss; Isaiah says God's word stands forever when grass and flowers fail.

column5: widow's garment must not be pledged
column6: The commentary joins truthful judgment to the restraint of collateral; Deuteronomy forbids perverting the vulnerable person's justice and taking a widow's garment as a pledge.

column5: just weights required in trade
column6: The commentary's market meets truthful, unswerving measure and the final scale; Leviticus orders honest balances, weights and measures.

column5: hears words but does not do them
column6: The commentary makes right works the secure building against the spider house; Jesus identifies the foolish sand builder as one who hears his words yet fails to act on them.

column5: wealthy life and hungry suffering reversed after death
column6: The commentary's stored plenty can end in loss beside unmet hunger; Abraham tells the rich man that Lazarus now receives comfort while he suffers, reversing their earthly shares.

column5: failure to feed hungry exposed in judgment
column6: The commentary places feeding on the difficult path toward final accountability; the judge condemns those who withheld food when he was hungry.

column5: wealth keeps a would-be follower from the path
column6: The commentary's hard climb requires releasing what is held; the rich man leaves Jesus grieving because he has many possessions after being told to give them away.

column5: uncertain riches versus secure trust
column6: The commentary's capital can be lost despite having been stored; Paul tells the wealthy to set hope on God rather than the uncertainty of riches.

column5: guard the entrusted deposit
column6: The commentary ends with an essence carefully held and conveyed; Timothy is again addressed as custodian of what has been entrusted to him, a separate recurrence from 2 Timothy 1:14.

column5: completed race and retained faith
column6: The commentary turns spent time into a sustained course ending with what remains; Paul says he has finished the race and kept the faith.

column5: day of just judge and kept reward
column6: The commentary's decisive day confronts a person's completed work; Paul expects a crown on that day from the righteous judge after retaining faith in 2 Timothy 4:7.

column5: love itself acts patiently
column6: The commentary treats patience as a communal virtue maintained between people; Paul calls love patient, placing endurance in a relationship rather than isolated self-control.

column5: love binds the group into completeness
column6: The commentary's rope scene turns separate people into a fitted company; Paul calls love the bond of perfection over the community's other virtues.

column5: unfruitful branch cast away and burned
column6: The commentary's loss links failing fruit and fire; Jesus says a branch that does not abide is thrown out, withers and is burned.

column5: joined vine branches bear fruit
column6: The commentary joins fruitful work to secure belonging; Jesus describes branches bearing much fruit only while abiding in the vine, making connection the source of yield.

column5: deeds follow the dead after labour ends
column6: The commentary sees an end of working time followed by assessment of what was preserved; Revelation promises rest from labour while the dead believers' works accompany them.

column5: own recollection: Arabic الصالحات / Hebrew צלח
column6: The commentary says good deeds fit and yield value; the psalm says the tree-like righteous person prospers in what he does, a possible sound and semantic cognate between source wording صلح and Hebrew צלח.

column5: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Hebrew חסר
column6: The commentary's loss is a dwindling principal; this proverb says possessive withholding leads to want, using Hebrew מחסור from חסר, a plausible but unverified cognate of the source's خسر.

column5: own recollection: Arabic خسر / Biblical Aramaic חסיר
column6: The commentary's losing human is found light in a balance; Daniel's Aramaic verdict says the king was found lacking, with חסיר plausibly corresponding to source wording خسر; the historical cognacy needs checking.

column5: own recollection: Arabic عمل / Hebrew עמל
column6: The commentary's right work should remain while spent life can be lost; Ecclesiastes hates toil that must be left to a successor, using עמל, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عمل with a darker sense.

column5: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
column6: The commentary joins pressing, withholding and rain; Solomon speaks of heaven being shut so that rain does not fall, using עצר, a possible cognate of source wording عصر whose sense here is restraint, not fruit pressing.

column5: own recollection: Arabic عصر / Hebrew עצר
column6: The commentary pairs squeezing with detention; Manoah asks the visitor to remain, using Hebrew עצר for holding someone back, a possible consonantal cognate of source wording عصر whose relationship needs verification.

column5: bread for hungry and clothing for naked
column6: The commentary's hard ascent includes concrete food and freedom for the vulnerable; Tobit instructs his son to give bread to hungry people and clothing to those without it.

column5: deliver oppressed person from oppressor
column6: The commentary's way over the steep rise frees a captive; Sirach instructs the reader to deliver an oppressed person from the oppressor and not shrink from judging a case.

column5: share possessions with a brother
column6: The commentary's exchange of sustaining things makes individuals a community; the Didache tells a believer to share possessions with a brother and avoid calling them exclusively one's own.

column5: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
column6: The commentary's haqq includes right judgment; Wisdom says rulers decree justice using חקק, consonantally close to source wording حق, though the historical relation between right and engraved decree is uncertain.

column5: own recollection: Arabic حق / Hebrew חקק
column6: The commentary expects an unswerving claim of right; Isaiah condemns rulers who decree unjust decrees using חקק, a possible cognate of source wording حق that also shows a contrary use of legal authority.
